source.title: Large scale analysis of generalization error in learning using margin based classification methods

record.tranche_reason: The study tests a double-descent prediction-error curve using an asymptotic replica analysis and finite simulations for margin classifiers in a random-features setting, rather than reproducing the original study's method.
record.gate_note: Figure 6 is the reported test-error sweep and is included below. The cited double-descent results from other papers are not rows. Figure 7 compares classifiers with optimally tuned regularization, but the text does not state whether a double-descent peak is present there. Epoch and sample-size sweeps are not reported.
record.test_reason: The study derives asymptotic test error for PLR, SVM and DWD on random-features data using the replica method, checks it against finite simulations, and reports a double-descent curve in p/n. This is a different method aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors reproduce double descent for PLR, SVM and DWD under the random-features (two-layer, random first layer) covariance, with the test error peaking at the critical p/n where the classes become linearly separable.
record.recipe_differences: Uses replica-based asymptotic analysis and finite simulations for margin classifiers on a random-features representation, rather than the original studies' methods; the first-layer weights are random.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sweep fixes tau at 10^-4, sign activation, and n/d = 3. The study also considers other settings and optimally tuned tau elsewhere, but does not describe a double-descent result for those settings.
record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
record.problems: The double-descent values are presented in a figure rather than tabulated. The text reports simulations based on 20 samples, but does not state uncertainty for Figure 6. The evidence comes from one random-features data setting and a fixed small regularization parameter.

untested.parts: Only one data model (sign-activation random features, n/d=3) and three linear margin classifiers at near-zero regularization (tau=1e-4); no other model classes.
No sweep of learned deep network size.
No sample-size sweep reported as test error near the threshold.
No label-noise manipulation. Figure 7 shows optimally tuned curves, but the text does not say whether the peak disappears.

missing.what: Test error versus p/n for the three classifiers at optimally tuned tau (n/d=2 and 3). This could show whether the peak vanishes under optimal regularization, but the text does not describe a peak; it would need reading from the figure.

record.verdict_notes: V1 is removed from the rows and labels because the trained model is a linear classifier on fixed random features, not a deep network grown in size. The peak location matches the interpolation and separability threshold. All evidence is from figures with no tabulated values, and Figure 6 does not state uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Does not sweep the size of a learned deep network; tests feature dimension in a random-features representation with random first-layer weights and margin-based classifiers.
Tests PLR, SVM, and DWD in one two-layer random-features data setting, not a broad range of model classes.
